answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making identity cost real, unrecoverable capital rather than free keys. Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if peers catch it spinning up puppet accounts to vote or farm rewards; since the bond is calibrated against the payoff of a single honest epoch, a farm of clones must lock millions before it earns a cent. The register of bonds also acts as a beacon: duplicate collateral paths and shared funding wallets stand out like ivory scars on a dark field, so reviewers can prune them at first gale rather than after damage.
